357590.title: Grazian–Monetta nilpotency conjecture for non-commuting graphs
357590.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and let $G=P\times A$ be a finite group where $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$ is non-abelian and $A$ is an abelian $p'$-group. Let $H$ be a finite group whose non-commuting graph is isomorphic to that of $G$, and suppose that $|Z(G)|\geq |Z(H)|$. **Grazian–Monetta conjecture.** Then there is a prime $q$ such that

$$
H=Q\times B,
$$

where $Q\in\operatorname{Syl}_q(H)$ is non-abelian and $B$ is an abelian $q'$-group. In particular, $H$ is nilpotent. This conjecture concerns the remaining case of determining whether a group with a non-commuting graph isomorphic to that of a finite nilpotent group must itself be nilpotent, under the additional condition on the orders of the centers; the source gives no resolution.

Shahverdi, Journal of Algebra 642 (2024), Theorem 1.3 states the exact P times A to Q times B conclusion with the same center-size hypothesis. Indexed primary theorem text located; publisher full proof not downloaded because ScienceDirect is inherited denied.

357600.title: The Aharoni–Korman conjecture for ordered sets without infinite antichains
357600.statement: Let $P$ be an ordered set with no infinite antichains, and let $k$ be a positive integer. Aharoni and Korman's conjecture asserts that there are $k$ chains $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ and a partition of $P$ into antichains $(A_i:i\in I)$ such that each $A_i$ intersects $\min(|A_i|,k)$ of the chains $C_j$. The conjecture generalizes the assertion that one chain can meet every part of a partition into antichains. The instance $k=1$ is known for well-founded ordered sets with every level finite; the paper verifies the full conjecture for posets whose incomparability graph is locally finite, and consequently for $(3+1)$-free posets with no infinite antichains.

357636.title: Uniqueness of binary phylogenetic trees from their $A_k$ alignments
357636.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 3}$, let $X$ be a taxon set, and let $T$ and $\widetilde{T}$ be binary phylogenetic trees on $X$. For a binary phylogenetic tree $T$, let $A_k(T)$ denote the set of binary characters requiring precisely $k$ nucleotide substitutions on $T$. **Uniqueness conjecture.** If $|X|\geq 2k+3$ and $T\not\cong\widetilde{T}$, then

$$
A_k(T)\neq A_k(\widetilde{T}).
$$

The claim would close the gap between the known counterexamples through $2k+2$ leaves and the paper's positive result for at least $4k$ leaves. It remains open in the source.

357745.title: The 3/2n flip-distance conjecture for non-crossing spanning trees
357745.statement: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be non-crossing spanning trees on the same set of $n$ points. A **flip** replaces one edge of a non-crossing spanning tree by another edge so that the result is again a non-crossing spanning tree. **The 3/2n flip-distance conjecture.** There is a flip sequence between any pair of non-crossing spanning trees of length at most $\frac{3}{2}n$. This would improve the general upper bound on flip distance and match the known lower bound up to an additive constant; the conjecture remains open, although the bound is proved in several special cases, including when one of the trees is a path or a nice caterpillar.

357791.title: The counting circuit double cover conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
357791.statement:
Let $G$ be a **bridgeless cubic graph** with $n$ vertices. A **circuit double cover** is a family of circuits covering every edge of $G$ exactly twice. **The counting circuit double cover conjecture.** The graph $G$ has at least

$$

circuit double covers. This strengthens the classical Cycle Double Cover Conjecture by asserting an exponential lower bound for cubic graphs; the source reports an infinite class attaining the bound, while the conjecture itself is presented as unresolved.

357850.title: Roudneff's conjecture on complete cells in pseudohyperplane arrangements
357850.statement:
Let $H(d,n)$ be an arrangement of $n$ pseudohyperplanes in the real projective space $\mathbb{P}^d$, and call a $d$-cell **complete** if it is bounded by every pseudohyperplane. For an oriented matroid of rank $r$ on $n$ elements, let $C_{r-1}(n)$ denote the number of complete cells in the cyclic arrangement of dimension $r-1$ with $n$ hyperplanes. **Roudneff's conjecture.** Every rank $r$ oriented matroid $\mathcal{M}$ on $n\geq r+1$ elements has at most

$$
2C_{r-1}(n)
$$

complete cells. Equivalently, every arrangement of $n\geq 2d+1\geq 5$ pseudohyperplanes in $\mathbb{P}^d$ has at most

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{d-2}\binom{n-1}{i}
$$

complete cells. The conjecture is known for $d=2,3$, for arrangements arising from Lawrence oriented matroids, and, by this paper's main theorem, for $d=4$.

358018.title: Rigidity conjecture for 4-connected symmetric simplicial 2-circuits
358018.statement:
Let $({\cal S},*)$ be a ${\mathbb Z}_2$-symmetric simplicial $2$-circuit. The graph $G({\cal S})$ is **4-connected** when it remains connected after deleting any set of at most three vertices, and it is **non-planar** when it cannot be embedded in the plane. A point group $\Gamma_{1,3}$ acts on $\mathbb R^3$ as specified by the paper, and $\Gamma_{1,3}$-rigidity means rigidity respecting this symmetry.

**Rigidity conjecture.** If $G({\cal S})$ is 4-connected and non-planar, then $G({\cal S})$ is $\Gamma_{1,3}$-rigid in $\mathbb R^3$.

This conjecture would characterize the exceptional non-rigid symmetric simplicial 2-circuits described by the insertion construction. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

$$
\{k\in\mathbb{C}:|\operatorname{Im}k|<C\}

358220.title: Sokal–Zeng's J-fraction conjecture for record-and-cycle permutation polynomials
358220.statement:
Let $\widehat{Q}_n(x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2,u_1,u_2,v_1,v_2,\mathbf{w},\lambda)$ be the permutation polynomials defined by weighting the record-and-cycle statistics, with $\mathbf{w}^{\boldsymbol{\rm fix}(\sigma)}=\prod_{i\in {\rm Fix}}w_{{\rm psnest}(i,\sigma)}$. **Sokal–Zeng's conjecture.** After specialising $v_1=y_1$, the ordinary generating function has the J-type continued fraction with coefficients

$$
\gamma_0=\lambda w_0,
$$

$$
\gamma_n=[x_2+(n-1)u_2]+[y_2+(n-1)v_2]+\lambda w_n\quad(n\geq1),
$$

$$
\beta_n=(\lambda+n-1)[x_1+(n-1)u_1]y_1.
$$

Equivalently, the continued fraction is the one displayed in the source statement. The conjecture concerns a multivariate refinement of permutation statistics and predicts an explicit continued-fraction expansion for its generating function.

358308.title: Léveque–Maffray–Trotignon conjecture on 4-coloring ISK4-free graphs
358308.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, undirected graph. A subdivision of $K_4$ is obtained by replacing the edges of $K_4$ with independent paths of length at least one between their end vertices; write $\text{ISK}_4$ for a graph isomorphic to such a subdivision. The graph $G$ is **ISK4-free** if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to a subdivision of $K_4$.

**Léveque–Maffray–Trotignon conjecture.** Every $\text{ISK}_4$-free graph is $4$-colorable.

Léveque, Maffray, and Trotignon showed that the chromatic number of $\text{ISK}_4$-free graphs is bounded by a constant, and no example with chromatic number at least $5$ was known when they proposed this conjecture. The conjecture is proved in the present paper for graphs containing a $K_{1,2,3}$, but its general status is not resolved here.

358355.title: Hyperplane covering conjecture for the permutohedron
358355.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the permutohedron with vertex set contained in the hyperplane

$$
H_0\colon \sum_{i=1}^n x_i={{n+1}\choose 2}.
$$

Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be affine hyperplanes different from $H_0$ whose union contains the vertex set of $P_n$. **Hyperplane covering conjecture.** If $n$ is odd, then $m\ge n$; if $n\ge 4$ is even, then $m\ge n-1$. This conjecture asserts that the explicit covers described in the paper are extremal; its resolution is not provided in the source.

358391.title: The totally odd strong immersion conjecture
358391.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\chi(G)$ for its chromatic number. A **totally odd strong immersion** is a totally odd immersion whose terminals do not occur as interior vertices on the paths representing edges. Let $K_t$ denote the complete graph on $t$ vertices.

**Totally odd strong immersion conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $\chi(G)\ge t$ contains a totally odd strong immersion of $K_t$.

This is presented as a strengthening of Churchley's conjecture, motivated by the paper's proof for line graphs of constant-multiplicity multigraphs. The general conjecture remains open.
358391.review_depth: Source arXiv:2305.07752v1, Conjectures 2/4, Theorems 3/6/8 checked. The line-graph proof supplies strong odd immersions only in the stated subclass.
358391.attempts: Dropping strongness or oddness changes the target; extending the source line-graph mechanism to general graphs would require a substantial new theorem. No routine bridge or new finite obstruction found.
358391.remaining_lemma_or_limit: Need a graph with chromatic number t and no totally odd strong K_t immersion, or a full-scope routing theorem.

358524.title: Matching conjecture for upset-decomposable modules
358524.statement:
Let $M$ and $N$ be upset decomposable persistence modules, where an upset decomposable module is a direct sum of upset modules. **The upset matching conjecture.** There is a constant $c\geq 1$ such that, for any $\epsilon$-interleaved upset decomposable modules $M$ and $N$, there is a $c\epsilon$-matching between $M$ and $N$.

This is the restriction of the paper's main conjecture to upset decomposable modules. The paper presents it as an open conjecture and relates it to the existence of common approximate refinements.
358524.review_depth: All three source versions retained. Current Conjecture 6.5 has pointwise finite-dimensional upset decomposable modules; Definitions 6.6/6.9 and Theorem 6.17 relate it to fixed-field constrained invertibility.

358525.title: Weakening conjecture for compatible-inclusion problems
358525.statement:
Let $c\geq 1$ be an odd integer, and let $(P,Q)$ be a compatible-inclusion problem, with its $c$-weakening defined by retaining directed edges represented by paths of length at most $c$. **The compatible-inclusion weakening conjecture.** There is an odd integer $c\geq 1$ such that, for any compatible-inclusion problem $\mathcal{P}$, if $\mathcal{P}$ has a solution, then the $c$-weakening of $\mathcal{P}$ has a simple solution.

This is a combinatorial reformulation related to the upset matching conjecture. The paper notes that the case $c=3$ weakens a conjecture from the author's PhD thesis, but the supplied text gives no resolution of the present conjecture.
